headline_summary: Copper extended losses for a third session toward $6.50/lb as hot US inflation fueled Fed rate-hike expectations, but strikes at Escondida and Centinela plus weather disruption at Codelco's El Teniente capped declines; data-center and grid demand remains supportive.

Brent held near $105.92/bbl after a tanker was sunk in the Strait of Hormuz and the US drew up strike plans on Iran; an 8mn bbl EIA crude draw supported prices while potential shadow-fleet sanctions easing and IEA emergency releases capped gains.
WTI jumped about 3% to $97.97/bbl, its highest in three weeks, as traders priced renewed Hormuz shipping attacks and a larger-than-expected 8mn barrel US crude inventory draw.

Henry Hub held near $3.21/MMBtu after a smaller-than-expected 67 Bcf storage injection, with Lower 48 output down to 110.8 Bcfd on hurricane-related shutdowns and pipeline disruptions; milder weather and softer LNG feedgas flows restrained the bullish case.

TTF paused near EUR 85.19/MWh after a rally to multi-year highs as Hormuz disruptions choke Middle East LNG (about 20% of global exports); EU storage at 74%, below seasonal norms, with a cold snap forecast for northeastern Europe next week.

Aluminum slid to $2,985/t, a YTD low erasing the war rally, as the dollar firmed, EGA restarted a quarter of Al Taweelah smelter and Chinese alloy exports doubled y/y; LME stocks at a century low still signal off-screen physical tightness.

Zinc SHG Rotterdam premium surged to $330/t (from $217.50/t in March) with spot concentrate TCs at a record-low -$115 to -$150/t in China, as war-hit supply chains and record-low TCs dominate pre-LME Week positioning.

Chinese lithium carbonate slumped 3.56% to CNY 104,400/t, a near 10-month low, after an SMM methodology change revealed Chinese stockpiles double prior estimates, Australian restarts (Bald Hill, Finniss) added supply, and the EU moved to cap Chinese hybrid EV imports.
FCPO fell 2.21% to MYR 4,596/t as record MPOB inventories of 3.51mn tonnes and weaker Dalian edible oils weighed, though 33-37% higher Oct 1-10 exports and Indian festive buying provided a floor.

November soybeans broke key support at $12.69 3/4 and the 50-day MA, closing at $12.63 after a 13-month-low NOPA crush of 196.3mn bu; continued Chinese buying (800,000t in two days) only partially offset harvest pressure.
EU carbon permits slipped 1.49% to EUR 85.84 in lacklustre trade as gloomy eurozone industrial production data, weaker gas prices and milder forecast weather curbed compliance buying.

BDI slumped 4.57% to 2,545, its lowest since June 30 and ninth straight session of declines, as capesize rates plunged 8.5% to a six-month low and panamax fell 2.2% on weak iron ore and coal cargo demand.
